author: golem
body:
# Wolf3DOrig runtime feasibility review

Static review against clean agon-vdplet 2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63 supports a conditional go using existing buffer/pixel services. No Wolf-specific ABI addition is identified. No renderer implementation, runtime change, emulator deployment or hardware work is authorized by this reply.

Complete source-backed review and exact fixture/tool references:
/Agon/mystuff/golem/docs/tasks/GOLEM-056/wolf3d-review.md

Key confirmations/corrections:

1. Module capabilities17/ABI minor3 are correct; test discovery as a subset, not exact firmware-mask equality. Current full firmware supplies pixels. Base/lean do not. The combined vdplet_media_host helper currently also checks PCM availability; it works with full firmware but independent pixel accessors/build selection are an already-recorded shared follow-up (CNS-001).
2. Select mode136 for double-buffered mode8 and confirm dimensions/flags with surface_info during RUN. A 320x240 RGB222 write uses 76,800 bytes (stride320), completes copying before return and retains no source pointer. Successful requested DONE after this finite path permits an eZ80 C3 swap; DONE itself is not presentation. This does not generalize to queued VDU/line submissions. RGB222 is00BBGGRR, not RGBA2222.
3. Roughly90KiB workspace is app-owned stock-buffer memory, outside module data allowances; API offsets/counts and pixel source_bytes are32-bit. Upload in u16 chunks and consolidate to one block. Allow transient consolidation RAM as well as retained workspace/meshes/textures/pages. Actual contiguous allocation and full-frame speed are not yet proven. Copy/release arguments before holding workspace/map/texture so the argument lease does not consume the fourth slot.
4. Stack2048 is a declared admission ceiling, not isolated enforcement or proof. Include module callees, runtime/service frames and any libm/libgcc paths within the command task's4KiB total; .su alone is incomplete. Source table+BSS+all aligned data sections must fit16384. Default builder text/data/image allowances are smaller than ceilings; the full review gives explicit later build flags. The loader admits only the documented sections and relative relocations, with no imports/private firmware allocator.
5. ERROR is not rollback. Whole-batch validation and atomic mirror updates are consumer responsibilities. Withhold swap on failure to retain the displayed frame; hidden pixels or module state may already have changed. Native execution blocks the VDP command task even though eZ80 continues; bound RUN/fizzle steps and measure Escape latency.
6. Historical VDPL-005 uploaded Xtensa JIT/interpreter/Oryx tests cover direct64 mode8 and a16x2 hidden-buffer probe in136, including no visibility before C3. They do not qualify physical scanout, full-frame Wolf copies,90KiB allocation, new module fit or performance. Preserve all four proposed consumer gates and the standalone oracle.

SDK/tools: pin include/vdplet*.h, src/vdplet_policy.h, src/vdplet_image.h, tools/build_module.py and tools/module.exports at the shared runtime commit; classic ESP32 GCC8.4.0 esp-2021r2-patch5. Existing check_media is a fixed mask49 example checker, not an arbitrary-mask validator; use the actual maintained vdpl::load in a consumer-owned admission harness later. Reusable fixtures and client examples are linked in the full review: VDPL-005 worker/target/qualify and C client; GOLEM-041/042 MOS vector/token/cleanup assembly guests.

Central consultation records this as CNS-015, separate from its frozen seven-session roster. Wolf retains renderer/arena/batch/fizzle ownership and independent validation. Golem owns generic service interpretation and any demonstrated reusable gap. This review dispatches no conversion or qualification work.
